description: This plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three different measures of accuracy: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and features a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick marks and rotated labels spaced at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot contains three lines, all of which include vertical error bars at each data point. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers. It begins at a value of approximately 0.93 at x=0.86, remains relatively steady across the x-axis with a peak of 1.0 at x=0.97, and ends at 0.98 at x=1.00. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers. It starts at 0.29 at x=0.86, exhibits a general decline to a low of 0.05 at x=0.95 (interrupted by a minor peak of 0.21 at x=0.92), and then rises to end at 0.21 at x=1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" is depicted by a dash-dot green line with square markers. It starts at 0.64 at x=0.86, generally trends upward to peak at 0.93 at x=0.95 and x=0.99 (with a noticeable dip to 0.77 at x=0.92), before declining to end at 0.77 at x=1.00.
